newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude, Ventritex cut merger value terms.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude, Ventritex cut merger value terms.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc and Ventritex Inc said Monday they had agreed to amend the terms of their merger by lowering the share-exchange ratio.
Under the new terms, each outstanding share of Ventritex will be converted into 0.5 share of St. Jude Medical, giving the deal a value of about $365 million.
Originally, each Ventritex share was to be converted into 0.6 share of St. Jude Medical.
The companies said they had agreed to the change to reflect the impact on Ventritex's business of component failures in its Cadence model V-110 implantable cardioverter defibrillator.
Ventritex has reported the deaths of three recipients of its defibrillators implants, which regulate heartbeat.
The companies said the amended merger pact also modifies certain covenants and conditions in the original agreement and make it "highly likely" that the merger will go ahead.
St. Jude Medical said it continues to work with the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and expects a completion of the antitrust review process shortly.
